memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob was angry and took Laban to task. 'What is my crime?' he asked Laban. 'How have I wronged you that you hunt me down? Now that you have searched through all my goods, what have you found that belongs to your household? Put it here in front of your relatives and mine, and let them judge between the two of us. I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten rams from your flocks. I did not bring you animals torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for whatever was stolen by day or night. This was my situation: The heat consumed me in the daytime and the cold at night, and sleep fled from my eyes. It was like this for the twenty years I was in your household. I worked for you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks, and you changed my wages ten times. If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, you would surely have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my hardship and the toil of my hands, and last night he rebuked you.'" - Gen 31:36-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
All the pent-up hurt of twenty years finally pours out of Jacob. He describes the brutal cost of those years: scorching heat by day, freezing cold by night, sleepless nights guarding the flocks, bearing losses out of his own pocket, and wages changed ten times. He had served with everything he had, and been repaid with exploitation. It is a raw, honest cry of a man who has laboured long under unfair treatment.

But the heart of Jacob's speech is this: "God has seen my hardship and the toil of my hands." That is where Jacob finds his footing. Even when no one else acknowledged his suffering, God had seen every hard day. Nothing had escaped the Lord's notice.

This is a profound comfort for anyone who feels their labour and pain go unseen. The exhausting work no one thanks you for, the sacrifices no one notices, the injustices no one acknowledges — God has seen them all. Not one drop of your sweat or one of your tears has been overlooked by Him.

Our God is the God who sees. Jesus assures us that even a cup of cold water given in His name is noticed, and nothing done for Him is ever wasted (Matt 10:42; Heb 6:10). When you feel unseen and unappreciated, lift your eyes. The One whose opinion matters most has seen it all, and He will not forget.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I feel my labour or pain has gone unseen?
2. How does it comfort me that "God has seen"?
3. Can I keep serving faithfully, trusting God to notice what others miss?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You see my hardship and the toil of my hands, even when no one else does. When I feel unseen, remind me that nothing done for You is ever overlooked. Amen.
